samuel2.24.p1.b1.text: Again the anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and He stirred up David against them, saying, “Go and take a census of Israel and Judah.”

samuel2.24.p1.b2.text: Go now throughout the tribes of Israel from Dan to Beersheba and register the troops, so that I may know their number.

samuel2.24.p1.b3.text: But why does my lord the king want to do such a thing?

samuel2.24.p1.b4.text: Nevertheless, the king’s word prevailed against Joab and against the commanders of the army.

samuel2.24.p2.b1.text: They crossed the Jordan … Then they went to Gilead … and around to Sidon. They went toward the fortress of Tyre … Finally, they went on to the Negev of Judah, to Beersheba.

samuel2.24.p2.b2.text: At the end of nine months and twenty days, having gone through the whole land, they returned to Jerusalem.

samuel2.24.p2.b3.text: In Israel there were 800,000 men of valor who drew the sword, and in Judah there were 500,000.

samuel2.24.p3.b1.text: After David had numbered the troops, his conscience was stricken

samuel2.24.p3.b2.text: I have sinned greatly in what I have done. … for I have acted very foolishly.

samuel2.24.p3.b3.text: When David got up in the morning, a revelation from the LORD had come to Gad the prophet, David’s seer …

samuel2.24.p3.b4.text: Do you choose to endure three years of famine in your land, three months of fleeing the pursuit of your enemies, or three days of plague upon your land?

samuel2.24.p4.b1.text: I am deeply distressed. Please, let us fall into the hand of the LORD, for His mercies are great; but do not let me fall into the hands of men.

samuel2.24.p4.b2.text: So the LORD sent a plague upon Israel from that morning until the appointed time,

samuel2.24.p4.b3.text: … seventy thousand of the people from Dan to Beersheba died.

samuel2.24.p5.b1.text: But when the angel stretched out his hand to destroy Jerusalem, the LORD relented from the calamity and said to the angel who was destroying the people,

samuel2.24.p5.b3.text: At that time the angel of the LORD was by the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.

samuel2.24.p6.b1.text: When David saw the angel striking down the people, he said to the LORD,

samuel2.24.p6.b2.text: Surely I, the shepherd, have sinned and acted wickedly. But these sheep, what have they done?

samuel2.24.p6.b3.text: Please, let Your hand fall upon me and my father’s house.

samuel2.24.p7.b1.text: Go up and build an altar to the LORD on the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.

samuel2.24.p7.b2.text: When Araunah looked out and saw the king and his servants coming toward him, he went out and bowed facedown before the king.

samuel2.24.p7.b3.text: To buy your threshing floor … that I may build an altar to the LORD, so that the plague upon the people may be halted.

samuel2.24.p7.b4.text: … Here are the oxen for a burnt offering and the threshing sledges and ox yokes for the wood.

samuel2.24.p8.b1.text: No … I insist on paying a price, for I will not offer to the LORD my God burnt offerings that cost me nothing.

samuel2.24.p8.b2.text: So David bought the threshing floor and the oxen for fifty shekels of silver.

samuel2.24.p8.b3.text: And there he built an altar to the LORD and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings.

samuel2.24.p8.b4.text: Then the LORD answered the prayers on behalf of the land, and the plague upon Israel was halted.
